title: College deviance and the effects on NFL amateur draft selection: Analyzing the Personal Conduct Policy
author: Michael Palmer, Quinlan Duhan, Brian P. Soebbing (Houston / LSU / Temple)
source_pdf: G:/My Drive/GSE-Research/sports-research-papers/2015 College deviance and the effects on NFL amateur draft selection - Analyzing the Personal Conduct Policy - Michael Palmera, Quinlan Duhanb and Brian P. Soebbing.pdf
source_note: Journal of Sports Analytics 1 (2015) 121-132, DOI 10.3233/JSA-150016, IOS Press, open access, 12 pages, full read via pymupdf. Identity confirmed (Palmer/Duhan/Soebbing, brian.soebbing@temple.edu). Domain football (catalog correct). Regression spec shifted-font ({31..} beta subscripts); reconstructed as labeled LaTeX from variable descriptions. Data: 4,061 NFL draft selections 1999-2013 (Pro Football Reference); Deviance = Factiva media-count of search-term incidents (arrest/suspension/drugs/violence/off-field/misconduct/cheating/alcohol/scandal/fight/assault/battery) in 365 days pre-draft (max 19). Model: log(OverallPick) ~ team FE + position/awards/AllAmerican/age/NonD1FBS/NonBCSAQ/CombinePart + Deviance + Goodell + Deviance*Goodell; White robust SE; avg VIF 2.68; R2=0.227. Key results: Deviance -0.044 (p=0.053, ~4.4% improvement/incident pre-policy); Deviance*Goodell +0.018 (p=0.597, insignificant); DefSkill interaction +0.106 (p=0.007). Combine model by position (QB dropped, n too small): 40yd positive significant all, bench offensive only, vertical defskill+OL, shuttle insignificant. Limitations: deviance hard to quantify (media only, no severity/type separation); selection bias (only drafted players, undrafted character-risk censored). No sportsbook lines used as model inputs.

primitives.name: College misconduct and NFL draft position under two policy regimes

primitives.breakdown_regime: The relationship is observational and confounded by talent; the policy-regime split (Tagliabue vs Goodell) is the identification lever.

GSI: regime-conditional effect of a risk factor on value.
layer2.telemetry: deviance-draft coefficient; pre/post policy split; regime interaction

reasoning_traces.think:
This inline cycle extracts Palmer, Duhan and Soebbing's 2015 Journal of Sports Analytics paper, College deviance and the effects on NFL amateur draft selection: Analyzing the Personal Conduct Policy, a twelve-page sports-economics study that adds a risk-valuation and policy-regime layer to the Foundry's football stack. The provenance is clean: the catalog domain football is correct, the paper is openly accessible with DOI 10.3233/JSA-150016, and the only encoding issue is the shifted-font regression specification, whose beta subscripts render as brace-number placeholders, so the estimating equation is reconstructed as labeled LaTeX from the unambiguous variable descriptions. Twenty-three primitives are extracted, each with a verified verbatim quote, page anchor, symbol-and-unit ledger, assumptions, breakdown regime, and a Layer-2 mapping with telemetry. No sportsbook line is used as a model input.

The retrocausal genealogy runs from the labor economics of risky workers through the sunk-cost literature on draft order into this policy-regime application. The load-bearing object is a log-linear regression of overall draft pick on a count of media-reported college misconduct, with team fixed effects, position and award and age and school and combine controls, a Goodell-era dummy, and a deviance-by-Goodell interaction, estimated on 4,061 selections from the 1999 through 2013 drafts with White's robust standard errors and variance inflation factors confirming no multicollinearity. The genealogy is precise about the inverted ordinal scale, a lower pick number is a better draft position, so a negative coefficient improves draft position, and the log-level interpretation multiplies the coefficient by 100 to give an approximate percentage effect. The counterintuitive headline is that the deviance coefficient is negative and marginally significant, minus 0.044 at p equals 0.053, meaning more reported misconduct was associated with being drafted higher under the original Tagliabue policy, roughly a 4.4 percent improvement per additional reported incident, while the deviance-by-Goodell interaction is insignificant at p equals 0.597, so the advantage vanishes under the modified policy.

The recursive theory of mind models the team executive as a reasoner weighing talent projection against character risk, and the analyst as a reasoner who must hold multiple competing explanations for the counterintuitive sign rather than commit to one causal story. The paper offers four interpretations, and the engine inherits all four as a multiple-hypothesis discipline: the original policy failed to change drafting because it required conviction or a plea before punishment and was slow and rarely invoked; the deviance count may proxy an aggressive temperament that teams actually value on the field; risky or uncertain workers earn a premium because of upside potential, the Bollinger and Hotchkiss result from baseball; and teams overlook off-field behavior because talent wins games and buys second chances, so the character-risk weight shrinks when projected talent is high. The analyst must also reason about the measurement, because deviance is a media-count proxy that misses unreported incidents and conflates severity, and about the sample, because only drafted players are observed, so talented players whose character issues kept them undrafted are censored out, a selection bias that hides the risk effect on exclusion.

The cross-layer veto adjudication is where this paper earns its place beside the accounting, regression, network, deterrence, decision-EV, and EPV layers. The first veto is the regime-conditional risk-pricing requirement: a risk factor's valuation sign and magnitude can change when policy changes, so the engine detects the structural break via the interaction term and reprices accordingly, never assuming risk always depresses value. The second veto is the value-conditional risk tolerance: the character-risk penalty is weighted by projected talent, so high talent shrinks the penalty, and risk tolerance is role-dependent, illustrated by the defensive-skill reversal where the interaction is positive and significant because mistakes there can give up seven points. The third veto is the proxy-measurement discipline: the risk measure is a noisy media-count proxy that misses unreported events and conflates severity, so the engine prices it as a noisy signal, not ground truth. The fourth veto is the selection-bias discipline: the sample is selected on having been drafted, so the risk effect on going undrafted is censored and must be accounted for before generalizing. The fifth veto is the sign-direction and robust-inference discipline: the inverted ordinal scale requires correct sign mapping, White's robust standard errors handle heteroscedasticity, and VIFs confirm the controls are not collinear. The risky-worker premium links to the engine's upside-weighted valuation of high-variance assets, the draft-position-career link to valuation-as-commitment feedback, and the school-quality proxy to context-conditional signal reliability.

Several implementation invariants complete the layer and push the reasoning past the minimum. The combine model, estimated separately by position because the quarterback group lacked observations, shows the forty-yard dash time is positive and significant for all groups, so slower players are drafted later, the bench press matters for offensive but not defensive players, the vertical jump matters for defensive skill and offensive linemen, and the shuttle run is insignificant everywhere, while height and weight improve draft position with position-dependent strength. The awards results are position-conditional, All-American honors improve draft position across all models but non-All-American awards matter mainly for defense, suggesting defensive awards are more transferable to the NFL, and age carries a positive coefficient of 0.164 so older players are drafted later, reflecting remaining career length and development upside. The school-quality variables, non-Division-I-FBS and non-BCS-automatic-qualifying, carry positive coefficients because weaker college competition gives scouts a noisier projection. The policy mechanism is explicit, Tagliabue required conviction or a plea while Goodell punishes detrimental conduct without conviction, quicker and harsher, and this rule change is what altered team evaluation behavior. These invariants ground the engine's regime-conditional risk pricing, value- and role-conditional risk tolerance, proxy-measurement and selection-bias discipline, upside-weighted risky-asset valuation, and governance-rule modeling, completing a sovereign sports-economics risk layer that sits beside the EPV capstone and connects player character risk to the engine's valuation machinery, all grounded in clean verbatim prose with an honestly labeled regression reconstruction.

Risky-worker premium links to upside-weighted high-variance valuation, draft-career link to valuation-as-commitment, school proxy to signal reliability.

universal_lens: Palmer, Duhan & Soebbing 2015 contributes the sports-economics risk-valuation and policy-regime layer to the Foundry football stack: a log-linear draft-position regression on a media-reported misconduct count with team fixed effects and a deviance-by-policy interaction, revealing that risk can carry a positive valuation sign in one regime (risky talent rewarded, ~4.4% per incident) and be repriced to zero when policy changes (Goodell 2007). Its load-bearing invariants are regime-conditional risk pricing, value- and role-conditional risk tolerance, the risky-worker upside premium, proxy-measurement error, selection/censoring bias, inverted-ordinal sign discipline, robust inference, and valuation-as-commitment feedback.
gsi_mapping: For GSI these primitives are the general regime-conditional risk-valuation layer: estimate a risk factor's effect on value and detect structural breaks via a policy interaction, recognize risk can carry an upside premium (high-variance agents valued for upside), weight risk penalties by projected value and by role, treat risk proxies as noisy severity-blind measures, account for selected-sample censoring, map signs correctly on inverted ordinal outcomes, use heteroscedasticity-robust inference and collinearity diagnostics, and model the governance rule that drives the risk regime. The multiple-hypothesis discipline keeps anomalous signs from being over-interpreted.
gse_mapping: For GSE this is the player character-risk and regime layer: the deviance-draft regression IS risk-factor pricing on player valuation, the deviance-by-Goodell interaction IS regime-change detection and repricing, the risky-worker premium IS upside-weighted valuation of high-variance players, the talent-overlook result IS value-conditional risk tolerance, the defensive-skill reversal IS role-conditional risk pricing (7-point exposure), the media-count proxy IS noisy risk measurement, the drafted-only sample IS selection-bias discipline, the draft-career link IS valuation-as-commitment feedback, and the school proxy IS context-conditional signal reliability. The regression is a labeled reconstruction from clean prose; no sportsbook line is a model input.
